note: THE BEST CRT+FVG CONFIGURATION MEASURED. Two changes take it from losing to working: a 0.25xATR buffer beyond the sweep extreme (net -0.0362 -> +0.0003, folds 2/5 -> 4/5) and the EMA21 reclaim on the entry bar (-> +0.1414 net, 61.3% WR, 5/5 folds). name: Gaussian trend filter (REJECTED): worse edge than EMA
note: Ehlers 4-pole Gaussian IIR swapped in for the EMA trend filter, the one idea worth compute from a web search on 2026-09-05 (everything else found was under 20 trades, one month long, or claimed Sharpe 10 on gold). Long-only, trail off, matched control, 5 folds, same bars and same SMA seed so both filters see identical warm-up. HEADLINE LOOKS LIKE A WIN AND IS NOT: gauss takes 710 trades to EMA's 543 and makes MORE total R (+118.69 vs +105.47), and on XAUUSD alone it posts +0.2605 R/trade at 5/5 folds against EMA's +0.1537 at 3/5. But its matched control rises with it - the extra trades are admitted in conditions where ANY entry did well. EDGE OVER CONTROL: EMA -0.0243, GAUSS -0.0866, so the Gaussian is 3.6x worse on the only column that matters, and on Gold it is the worst cell measured (-0.2424 against a +0.5029 control - the strategy captures half what a random entry in the same conditions would). Also loses BTCUSD outright (+0.0904 3/5 vs +0.2041 5/5) and drops pooled folds 5/5 -> 4/5. Default stays ema; the flag is opt-in and the ema path was verified byte-identical to the pre-change baseline before any comparison was run.

name: GC 5-day block bias (REJECTED): real short-side skill, wrong side
note: His strategy from the 2026-09-05 screenshots, transcribed rather than paraphrased: 5 daily bars vs the next 5, direction = close(last)-close(first); block1 down + block2 up -> sell into 80pc of block2 range; trigger an H1 close below the 12 EMA in LONDON; stop 1.5xATR14. Target was NOT specified so it was swept. NO TARGET MAKES IT PROFITABLE: RR 1.0/1.5/2.0/3.0/4.0 give -0.0619/-0.0596/-0.0192/-0.0304/-0.0821 R per trade, best at 2R and still negative, folds never better than 3/5. BUT THE FILTER IS REAL: against a matched control it is +0.1213 at 2R and +0.2247 at 3R, bigger than TK pullback long-only (+0.0352) and approaching FVG continuation (+0.2249). It is selecting gold shorts that lose far less than random gold shorts - skill at picking the least-bad short, not profit. The mirror settles the interpretation: block1 up + block2 down -> BUY gives +0.0408 strategy against a +0.1203 control, edge MINUS 0.0796, so the structure does not transfer to longs. Rejecting the strategy, not the finding.

name: Gold's directional base rate: random longs +0.12, random shorts -0.14
harness: node tasks/gc_block_bias.cjs --symbol XAUUSD --shorts 0 --longs 1   (read the CONTROL row)
note: Not a strategy - the measured base rate that explains why every short model in this ledger fails. The matched controls of the block-bias test are random entries with identical stop and target distances in the same conditions: LONG control +0.1203 R over 392, SHORT control -0.1405 R over 445. That is a 0.26R directional spread on XAUUSD at 1.5xATR stops and a 2R target. Any short strategy on gold starts a quarter of an R behind, which is the arithmetic behind TK v2 shorts at -0.0785 (1/5 folds) and the shadow short ledger at -18.15R over 243. It also sets the bar honestly: a gold short model needs an edge over control above roughly +0.14 merely to break even, and the best measured so far is +0.1213. Use this before proposing any short-side work.
